# Review

## Summary

The note defines its own comparison vocabulary well: predecessor, candidate and operative successor get a dedicated glossed list; experience-responsive retention is defined in the sentence that introduces it; non-regression, the target dimension and prior scope ("what that state could already do") are explained where they appear; and compounding is paraphrased in the following sentence.

The gaps are terms imported from linked notes. The note's subject, "software factory", and the concepts "factory development", "redesign class" and "open production family" are relied on without an inline gloss, and "learner boundary" is used in the opening well before its definition. Each forces the reader to follow a link or carry an unresolved term through the argument. Short inline glosses at first mention would resolve all of them without restructuring the note.

# Review

The note's main claim, taken from its title, description and the "Four declarations" paragraph, has three parts. A better-factory claim compares a predecessor with an operative successor. It uses an antecedent, scope-indexed assessment relation. Its evaluator location is declared separately from the learner boundary. Most side material in the note supports this claim.

The deployed-system paragraph places all operative machinery inside the compared states. That premise belongs to the relata. The "Neither claim entails the other" section separates improvement from learning attribution. That boundary is needed because the opening derives the better-factory claim from retention's silence about quality. The Scope bullets bound antecedence and the two-route reading. These stay.

The preserved-path section is the main branch. It is a sound consequence of scope indexing, but it is downstream of the declarations, not part of them. With the compounding contrast, it adds a second topic with its own evidence needs. It also forces a Scope concession about relations that permit retirement of prior capability. The last Scope bullet uses this clause to justify stating the structure for factories. If the section is rehomed, that bullet needs a different justification or can say that the structure is general.

The oracle paragraph is a smaller case. Its final clause supports the evaluator-location declaration. Its first two clauses open a branch that the note explicitly does not resolve.

The TODO line about "software house" is an editorial marker, not a branch. This criterion does not assess it.

# Review

## Summary

Most of the note's detail matches the work it does. One caveat outgrows its role through repetition.

## Assessment

The note sets out four declarations, and most of its supporting detail does real argumentative work:

- The interleaved-process example in **Measurement over snapshots** is needed. Without it, "a measurement boundary drawn on a continuous process" would stay abstract, and the contrast with candidate admission would lose its force.
- The list of machinery parts (prompts, code, tools, tests and so on) takes up one sentence. It also blocks the likely objection that fixed model weights rule out the comparison.
- The paragraph on preserving the factory-development path is short and keeps three things apart: preservation, editability and compounding. Each distinction stops a likely misreading.
- In **Neither claim entails the other**, the operator case and the capable-builder case are two distinct counterexamples to reading improvement as learning. The manipulation clause is the inference step that comes out of them. The paragraph is long, but each part carries a separate step.
- The oracle-problem paragraph uses three short clauses, one for each difficulty, and connects back to evaluator location. It is in proportion.

The overhang is in the caveat about what the declared relation does not establish. The note states it in the opening paragraph, again at the close of the antecedence paragraph, and twice more in Scope. The Scope bullets are the right home for it because they separate the two cases: no oracle, and dimensions that are declared correctly but still wrong. Each in-body restatement repeats the same point without adding a condition. Compressing them would shorten the note without weakening it. The reader still meets the caveat where it is fully qualified.

# Review

## Summary

Most chunks earn their space. These parts are not redundant: the three-term vocabulary, the two successor routes, the two-component relation with scope indexing, the split between preservation and compounding, the evaluator/boundary argument, and the 'Neither claim entails the other' section. Each one adds a distinction that a later part of the note relies on. Most Scope bullets also add something new: the retrospective-criterion admission, the retirement-permitting relation, routes as declarations rather than partitions, and the reach claim.

The redundancy comes from one pattern. The note restates one limit several times: the comparison is auditable but is not a verdict on factory quality. That limit appears in the opening paragraph, at the end of the antecedence paragraph, and in two Scope bullets. The note also lists its structure twice in the opening, and it justifies the preserved-path consequence a third time after the heading and derivation have already established it. The fix is to cut and fold, not rewrite. The closing sentence of the successor-routes section and the closing sentence of the evaluator section restate earlier points, but each turns them into a consequence that the next part uses. They therefore pass.

"Consumes the capacity for further improvement" and "closing the route" use "route" and "path" in the sense the note defines: the factory-development path. "A passing successor is cheap" means easy to obtain at that boundary, and the following clause explains why. "That is all antecedence buys" scopes the claim precisely. "Who was in the room" is a conventional idiom; the sentence contrasts it directly with the gating role. "Re-enters at the headline result rather than at a labelled input" is a compact contrast between two positions in the evidence chain, and the note uses that contrast.

# Friction check: better-factory claims compare operative states

**Central claim (one sentence):** A claim that a factory got better becomes determinate only when it compares the predecessor with the installed, depended-on successor under a scope-indexed relation (non-regression plus a named target) fixed before the development it judges, with evaluator location declared separately from the learner boundary.

## Filter
**Filter:** SURVIVES

The commitments to operative-state relata, an antecedent relation, scope-indexed non-regression and two successor routes can coexist. The claim makes the relation constrain auditability, not quality, and the Scope section limits its reach. The closest strain is between separately declared evaluator location and the admission route, where gating places the evaluator on the causal path. The note leaves that strain open as a question; it does not split the central claim into incompatible parts.

## Thinnest joints

The ranking follows how much of the structure rests on each joint and how little support it gets. The scope-indexing dichotomy ranks first. It is the only stated justification for indexing, and the preserved-path section builds on indexing, yet the sentence asserts both horns without argument. The preserved-path derivation ranks next because it presents a further requirement as a logical consequence. It holds only if the factory-development path is one of the declared dimensions. The evaluator-location joint depends on a causal reading of "gated", which the Scope section's descriptive reading of routes undermines. The oracle-problem and unfalsifiability joints point in the right direction but overreach their reasons. Joints left unsurfaced held up: candidates are excluded by definition, deployed-system scope follows from the linked note, and the experiment-contrast argument for attribution follows from its linked note.

## For the human
Look first at "unmeetable or vacuous": say concretely what non-regression over an unindexed scope would demand and why it fails. The scope-indexing and preserved-path sections depend on that answer.

# Critique: A better-factory claim compares operative states under an antecedent assessment relation

**Note:** kb/theory/a-better-factory-claim-compares-operative-states.md
**Central commitment:** A better-factory claim is determinate only when it declares four things. The relata are the predecessor and the installed, depended-on successor, not a candidate. The relation is fixed before the development and combines non-regression on the prior scope with a named target. The successor's route is either measurement or admission. Evaluator location is declared separately from the learner boundary.
**Critique mode:** claim
**Attack outcome:** partially lands

## Strongest case against it

The opponent is a practitioner of online experimentation and causal evaluation, such as an A/B-testing or counterfactual-evaluation engineer. On this view, "the successor is better than the predecessor" is a counterfactual claim. The question is how the successor performs on the same work under the same conditions, compared with the predecessor. Only a matched contrast can answer it: run both on shared tasks, or run them concurrently on randomized traffic.

The note makes the later relatum the installed, depended-on state and treats a staging comparison only as "evidence for that decision". That choice moves the comparison away from a matched contrast in two ways:

1. **Time separation confounds the result.** The operative successor is measured later than the predecessor, and the note's measurement route is a "measurement boundary drawn on a continuous process". On a "named production dimension", the later measurement takes place in a different environment. The task distribution has drifted. External models and tools may have changed. Because later work depends on the successor, the successor has itself shaped the work it is measured on. Antecedence stops post-hoc choice of dimensions. It does not stop the environment from passing the comparison for the factory. A successor that is no better can pass because the work became easier, and a better one can fail because the work became harder.
2. **The predecessor usually cannot be recovered.** The compared states "span the whole production environment", including prompts, artifacts, tools, workflows, tests and evaluators. In an interleaved process, that whole state is not normally kept as a runnable snapshot. Once it is superseded, the predecessor's side of the comparison is either a baseline recorded at declaration or a recollection. The note requires neither.

The opponent concludes that the defensible relata are runnable configurations compared on matched work, which is what the note calls candidates. Installation is a further fact about deployment and adds nothing to the comparison except confounds. The note's own sentence "Passing the comparison establishes improvement between the two states" is therefore false as written whenever the comparison is not matched.

## How the note engages it

**Partially engaged.** Several parts of the note limit the attack:

- The relation is fixed "while only the predecessor exists". On a natural reading, this includes measuring the predecessor's baseline at declaration. On a fixed, replayable suite, that covers the non-regression component and the recovery problem.
- The note grants that a staging comparison is evidence for the claim. It insists only that the claim's later term is the installed state. That position is consistent: the relata can be operative states while the evidence comes from a matched contrast. Taken as a claim about what the relata are, the note's main commitment survives. Installation does determine which state the claim is about, and a discarded candidate should not count.
- The Scope section admits that the framework "does not supply an oracle" and that a properly declared comparison can still measure the wrong thing. The first open question raises whether the prior scope can be specified for open-ended families.
- The note applies [an experiment identifies only the contrast it actually runs](./an-experiment-identifies-only-the-contrast-it-actually-runs.md), but only to attribution, meaning whether the factory learned.

Three things go unengaged. The note never applies the contrast principle to the improvement comparison itself. It does not say how the predecessor-side measurement is obtained in the measurement route. Its "Neither claim entails the other" section says that passing establishes improvement between the states. The attack lands on that sentence and on the missing predecessor-measurement requirement. It does not land on the choice of operative states as relata.

## Constructive findings

- Limit "Passing the comparison establishes improvement between the two states", or add a condition to it. Passing establishes improvement under the declared relation only when the comparison is matched. That means a predecessor baseline fixed at declaration on a replayable suite, or matched runs of both states. For production-dimension targets measured over time, say that environmental drift and the successor's own effect on later work are confounds the declarations do not remove.
- Add the predecessor-side measurement to what antecedence fixes. Declare the relation and also record the predecessor's measured standing on it at declaration time. Otherwise the measurement route compares a present measurement with nothing. This also turns part of the first open question into a concrete requirement.
- Bring the Scope bullet on successor routes into line with the evaluator-location section. State that whether an evaluator gated installation is a fact about the episode. Choosing a description cannot move a gating evaluator off the causal path.

## Secondary objections (optional)

- The note says the compared state includes evaluators and tests, but it does not say whose tests decide the relation. Antecedence implies the relation stays fixed even if the successor revises its own test suite, but the note does not state this. A reader could take a successor that rewrote its acceptance tests to be measured by them.
- The line `TODO! remove or update to use software house instead of software factory` signals a pending terminology change. If "software house" replaces "software factory", the note's title, the claim's name and the scope bullet that relies on factory development may all need revising. The critique judges the current factory wording.

# Premise decomposition: better-factory claim compares operative states

**Register:** claim
**Central commitment (one sentence):** A claim that a factory got better is determinate and auditable only when four things are declared: operative predecessor and successor states as relata, an antecedent scope-indexed relation, the route by which the successor arose, and an evaluator location separate from the learner boundary.

## Premises and counterexamples

The commitment rests on one premise per declaration and on the conditions that keep each one checkable. The first group makes the relata well defined. Improvement must be a separate claim from retention, candidates must be excluded, a successor must be fixable as one state, and the predecessor must stay measurable. The last premise is unstated and is the one the note most needs to add. The second group makes the relation determinate: antecedence must block post-hoc fitting, and the prior scope must be specifiable enough to check. The preserved-path consequence is derived from this group, so it depends on how 'scope' is declared. The third group separates evaluator location from the learner boundary. It needs the measurement/admission split to be causally clean, and it needs the route to be a fact the declaration records rather than one it chooses.

Each failure found can be repaired by adding a condition or narrowing a reading, and none forces the commitment itself to be withdrawn, so all are local. The pattern is the same across them. The note names the right declarations, but several are underspecified for checking: the scope, the measurement instances and the predecessor's availability. One Scope bullet also contradicts the body's causal account of evaluator location.

## For the human

Start with prior-scope specifiability. Over an open production family, the note's 'determinate' thesis depends on a declared scope proxy that it currently leaves as an Open Question.
